answer.rationale: With the contract expiring in 14 days, the 18% spend cut is the dominant constraint. Memory c2 confirms the low-cost vendor is already onboarded and performing, so there's no cold-start risk. Memory c6 shows multi-year leverage exists. Memory c4 shows negotiating at renewal yielded real margin last cycle. Renegotiating the incumbent (or leveraging the switch option) to extract the 18% reduction keeps delivery risk flat—no new vendor onboarding under the 14-day window, no dual-source complexity—while hitting the cost target. Switching primary in 14 days is too risky given the assembly line is at 94% with no buffer. Deferring is not viable with a hard expiry.
